correctness.rationale: The trace-decreasing no-detection generator is completely positive; positive on-site and edge jump rates force positivity improvement, hence a unique globally attracting Perron density for every m>=2, p>0, eta<1. Leaf permutations reduce the stationary eigenproblem exactly to the displayed five-variable matrix. Elimination is justified by lambda>-2p and Gamma>=4. An implicit-function argument near -p(1+eta) yields a positive eigenmatrix and all fixed-efficiency coefficients. The eta=xi/m crossover is obtained from the same scalar equations, with xi=0 checked exactly. The independent full Liouvillian construction and asymptotic checks pass 216 assertions in check_star.py; finite numerics are not used as proofs.

The comparison is at the level of model and claimed limits, not title matching; possible implicit coverage from broader quasi-stationary spectral theory is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper argues that postselection-induced peripheral localization can preserve quantum coherence in finite heterogeneous quantum networks. The star is a canonical degree-heterogeneous test family; exact hub suppression from O(m^-1) to O(m^-2) and aggregate-coherence collapse at O(m^-1) reveal an experimentally and conceptually relevant large-network boundary. The eta~1/m crossover gives a quantitative monitoring-strength scale separating unconditional-like and strongly suppressed hub probabilities, with the full coherent mixing parameter retained. This is not a value claim based merely on symbolic reduction or numeric computation.
